The words

To avert from men God's wrath
Jesus suffered in our stead;
By an ignominious death
He a full atonement made;
And by His most precious blood,
Brought us, sinners, nigh to God.

That we never should forget
This great Love on us bestowed,
He gave us His flesh to eat,
and to drink His precious blood;
All who sick and needy are
May receive in Him a share.

Hither each afflicted soul
May repair, though filled with grief;
To the sick, not to the whole,
the Physician brings relief;
Fear not, therefore, but draw nigh,
Christ will all your wants supply.

He who in self—righteousness
Fixes any hope or stay,
Has not on a wedding dress,
And with shame is sent away;
To the hungry, weary heart,
He will food and rest impart.

But examine first your case,
Whether you be in the faith;
Do you long for pard'ning grace?
Is your only hope His death?
Then, howe'er your soul's oppressed,
Come, you are a worthy guest.

He who Jesus' mercy knows, Is from wrath and envy freed;
Love unto our neighbor shows That we are His flock indeed;
Thus we may in all our ways Show forth our Redeemer's praise.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (E♭).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are by John Hus, first published in 1400. The English translation is by Christian Ignatius Latrobe (1789). The tune, GETHSEMANE, is by Richard Redhead (1853). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (1400): John Hus (1369–1415)
  • Translated (1789): Christian Ignatius Latrobe (1758–1836)
  • Music (1853): Richard Redhead (1820–1901)

Questions about To Avert from Men God's Wrath

What is the doh of To Avert from Men God's Wrath?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does To Avert from Men God's Wrath start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is To Avert from Men God's Wrath in the public domain?

Yes. John Hus died in 1415, Christian Ignatius Latrobe died in 1836, Richard Redhead died in 1901; the words were first published in 1789 and the music in 1853. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
